title: Microsoft Purview DLP: test files against all classifiers (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The roadmap details and both documented commands check out, but the briefing overstates permissions: Microsoft does not establish that everyone who can open the new test can submit files, and global administrators can view role groups without the separately stated Role Management requirement. Several details of the new testing workflow are also inferred rather than documented.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview is adding file testing on the main Classification page.
claims.quote: A new feature will be introduced on the main Classification page, allowing users to test files against all available classifiers to identify the presence of sensitive information.

claims.claim: The new test can evaluate files against all available classifiers for sensitive information.
claims.quote: allowing users to test files against all available classifiers to identify the presence of sensitive information.

claims.claim: Users can instead select one classifier for the new test.
claims.quote: Users will have the option to select a single classifier or run tests across all classifiers.

claims.quote: This capability is designed to help users identify sensitive content within files and troubleshoot classification issues more efficiently.

claims.claim: The existing per-type test is at Microsoft Purview portal > Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types > sensitive information type > Test.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types and choose the sensitive information type from the list to open the details pane. Choose Test.

claims.claim: Test-DataClassification -ClassificationNames <names> -TextToClassify <text> tests text for specified sensitive information types, not an uploaded file.
claims.quote: The ClassificationNames parameter specifies the sensitive information type that you want to find in the text specified by the TextToClassify parameter. Valid values are: Name; Id (GUID value). You can specify multiple values separated by commas.

claims.claim: Purview role-group membership is managed at Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit on the control bar. ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: Include the documented wizard-page heading in controls[1].ui.path and its rendered table path: 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users'.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user>" adds the user to the specified management role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group.

claims.claim: Viewing role groups needs the Role Management role.
claims.quote: To view Role groups in the Roles and scopes area in the Microsoft Purview portal, users need to be a global administrator or need to be assigned the Role Management role (assigned only to the Organization Management role group).
claims.fix: Replace 'Needs the Role Management role to view role groups' in controls[1].note and the rendered table with 'To view role groups, be a global administrator or have the Role Management role (assigned only to the Organization Management role group)'.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not say whether the new all-classifier test has the existing Test option's Exchange Online licence condition.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview file testing against all sensitive information classifiers licensing price meter prerequisites'; read SIT testing, Learn about SITs, Classifiers overview and Purview service description. No passage extends that condition to this new test.

claims.claim: The Classifiers overview itself names no licence.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the roadmap's all-classifier file-testing workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "test" "all classifiers" results matches file'; read Classifiers overview, SIT testing and Learn about SITs. Results describe per-type tests, training or on-demand scans, not the roadmap's main-page all-classifier test.

claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, you can access Classifiers under Information Protection, Data Loss Prevention, or DSPM (Data Security Posture Management).

claims.quote: The new Classifiers experience in Microsoft Purview is in preview and is available alongside the existing classification experiences. ... Features and functionality in the new experience might change before general availability.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not identify the roles that can run the new all-classifier test.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions; controls notes
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a tenant switch for the new all-classifier test; neither existing control row is documented as that switch.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "Classifiers" "test" "all" default permissions tenant enable file testing'; read Classifiers overview, SIT testing, Purview permissions and both cmdlet references. They describe testing and membership, not a new-test enable/disable switch.

claims.where: Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: No source describes the new test as changing existing behaviour or introducing a change to end users.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview classifiers uploaded file testing labels blocks moves deletes file policy test results'; read the roadmap, Classifiers overview and SIT testing. None states that the new file test changes existing user behaviour.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No source describes the new test as labeling, blocking, moving or deleting content.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview classifiers uploaded file testing labels blocks moves deletes file policy test results'; read the roadmap and SIT testing, and classification/simulation search excerpts. Actions described for scans or policies are not attributed to this new test.

claims.claim: Microsoft names no required administrator action for the new test's arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "file testing" "classifiers" GCC GCC High DoD file limits roles administrator action'; read the roadmap, Classifiers overview, SIT testing and Purview permissions. No rollout-specific administrator action for the new test is stated.

claims.claim: Anyone who can open the new test can submit a file to it.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "Classifiers" "test" "all" default permissions tenant enable file testing'; read Classifiers overview, Purview permissions and SIT testing. Page-access roles are documented, but opening the new test is not stated to confer permission to submit.
claims.fix: Replace 'Anyone who can open the test can submit a file to it' with 'Confirm who can submit files to the new test before widening access'. Keep the sample/redacted-file advice.

claims.claim: Testing all classifiers produces more results to read than testing one.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "test" "all classifiers" results matches file'; read Classifiers overview and SIT testing. The roadmap permits testing all classifiers but does not specify result presentation or guarantee more returned results.
claims.fix: Replace 'Testing against all classifiers produces more results to read than testing one' with 'Check how the new test presents results when all classifiers are selected'. Keep the advice to agree who interprets results.

claims.claim: Running tests and reading their results entails administrator or analyst time, presented as a cost Microsoft documents.
claims.quote: Upload a file and choose Test. ... On the Match results page, review the results and choose Finish. ... Perform the same steps for the second file.
claims.fix: Present the time cost as wiki analysis, not Microsoft's published cost: replace 'The cost Microsoft documents is therefore indirect: administrator and analyst time to run tests and read results' with 'Plan for administrator and analyst time to run tests and read results'. In the cost rationale, replace 'the cost Microsoft documents for the existing per-type Test option is an Exchange Online licence in the tenant, plus admin time' with 'Learn requires an Exchange Online licence in the tenant for the existing per-type Test option; plan for admin time to run tests'.

claims.claim: The new all-classifier test operates on an uploaded file.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "test" "all classifiers" results matches file'; read Classifiers overview and SIT testing. The roadmap says 'test files' without describing input selection; uploading is documented only for the existing per-type workflow.
claims.fix: Replace 'Purview is adding a file test that checks an uploaded file against one or all classifiers' in the summary with 'Purview is adding a file test against one or all classifiers'.

claims.claim: The new test checks why a document was or was not detected without first building or changing a policy.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview classifiers uploaded file testing labels blocks moves deletes file policy test results'; read Classifiers overview and SIT testing. The existing SIT procedure is independent of policy creation, but the new test's policy dependencies are not stated.
claims.fix: Replace 'A file test on the Classifiers page gives compliance and security teams a way to check why a document was or was not detected without building or changing a policy first' with 'The roadmap describes the new test as a way to find sensitive content and troubleshoot classification issues'.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The same sensitive information type can produce different detection results in email in transit, files at rest and files on managed devices.
claims.quote: The same sensitive information type can produce different results depending on where content is evaluated—for example, email in transit (Exchange), files at rest (SharePoint and OneDrive), and files on managed devices (Endpoint DLP).
